title: Python lightweight checkpoint protocol and event router for streaming chat
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a compact, forward-compatible checkpoint protocol plus an in-SDK event router to make streaming chat completions resumable, testable, and easy to integrate. Goal: provide a minimal surface for application authors that works across transports (SSE, websocket, http chunked) and supports idempotent retries, lightweight consumer commits, and sync/async parity in the Python SDK.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a ContextManager and async context that yields a StreamConsumer with commit()/checkpoint_token() methods
Checkpoints are compact opaque tokens <= 256 bytes representing stable fragment boundaries and KV-cache offsets
Resuming a stream with a checkpoint token restores observable behavior (no duplicate user-visible fragments) for common failure modes
Event router can demultiplex chat tokens to multiple named sinks and drop / retry policies are configurable
Unit and integration tests cover partial-fragment failure, duplicate events, and concurrent commit races
Performance: checkpointing adds <1% median latency for 99th percentile short requests in microbenchmarks
decisions: Use opaque base64 cursor tokens that encode sequence id, model-kv-offset, and a short integrity HMAC (KMS-managed) to allow offline verification
Commit semantics: consumer-side optimistic commit with server-ack fallback; SDK will surface commit success/failure and optionally auto-retry transient failures
Keep protocol v2 backwards-compatible: servers should accept older tokens; SDK will attempt a best-effort fast-path when token is present and fall back to full-context fetch
Expose a minimal API: StreamSession(stream_id, transport, consumer_factory, *, resume_token=None) + session.checkpoint() + consumer.commit()
Implement transport adapters for SSE and websocket; http-chunked adapter will reuse same contract via adapter shim
Telemetry: emit checkpoint_issued, checkpoint_applied, checkpoint_resume_failed, consumer_commit_latency metrics with tags for model, transport, and tenant
implementation_notes: Add StreamSession abstraction in py/sdk/streaming/session.py with both sync and async implementations sharing core helpers
Create CompactToken class to marshal/unmarshal base64 tokens; tokens contain version byte to allow evolution
EventRouter will be a pluggable object: DefaultEventRouter demuxes by event.type and conversation_id header; custom routers may be registered per-session
Backpressure: router exposes a throttled_sink helper that applies bounded asyncio.Queue for async paths and a blocking queue for sync paths with configured wait policy
Idempotency: each consumer should produce an idempotency_token per outbound action. SDK will attach a consumer_id in event envelopes to help server-side dedupe
Security: HMAC key rotation supported; tokens carry a key_id. Review with security for KMS integration and threat model
API ergonomics: provide lightweight high-level examples in docs/quickstarts and code-snippets for common patterns (single-consumer, fanout to webhook, checkpoint-on-flush)
test_plan: Unit tests for CompactToken encode/decode, including cross-version decode failures handled gracefully
Integration test harness with local SSE server and deterministic replay fixture to validate resume semantics
Chaos tests: kill connection mid-fragment, delay final fragment ack, insert duplicate events, assert no double-deliver to committed consumer
Load test: measure checkpoint overhead under 10k req/s synthetic workload; track 50/95/99 latencies with and without checkpointing
Fuzz test for malformed tokens to ensure SDK returns a resumable error rather than crashing
